observation.visible_scene: A stationary dark-colored SUV, heavily fire-damaged with blackened panels and a large patch of white foam/chemical residue on its side doors, parked on wet asphalt. A white pickup truck sits motionless in the background to the right, and a red hose lies along the bottom-left edge. Smoke or steam vents continuously from the damaged vehicle throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The SUV, its wheels, the white pickup, the house and distant sign remain at fixed pixel positions across all frames, indicating no object translation and no camera pan/zoom.
A vertical plume of smoke/steam rises from the roofline (above the B-pillar/rear window area) in every frame, with its thickness and exact outline fluctuating frame to frame.
A broader, lower cloud of smoke billows around the mid-to-lower side of the car (near the rear door and wheel arch), drifting and reshaping rather than moving as a rigid body.
The white residue on the body panels and the charred surfaces do not change shape or position; they are static material deposits, not moving objects.
By the later frames the roof plume appears somewhat thinner/more dispersed and the side cloud spreads slightly more horizontally, while the overall scene composition stays the same.
The red hose at the bottom-left remains in the same position and orientation throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the smoke/steam (active fire, residual heat, or applied extinguishing agent) is not shown.
What occurred before the first frame and after the last frame is unknown; the venting is already ongoing at t=0 and continues past the final frame.
Whether the white residue is extinguishing foam or chemical damage cannot be determined from the images alone.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain but background landmarks are pixel-stable, so the view is effectively static.
Distinguishing smoke from steam and identifying the exact venting source(s) on the vehicle is not possible from these frames.
Minor frame-to-frame differences in plume shape could be natural turbulence rather than a directional drift; no clear net translation of the cloud is established.
